chunks.title: `denext mobile`
chunks.text:
## `denext mobile`

Capacitor helpers (add: native capabilities; add-ota: over-the-air UI updates; dev: live reload; fingerprint: native-layer hash; assets / build / submit: icons, store builds, store uploads)

```sh
denext mobile <action> [args...] [options]

  denext mobile add <capability...>
                                Add the Capacitor plugins behind denext/mobile's
                                capability functions, then `npx cap sync`
  denext mobile add deep-links --scheme myapp --domain app.example.com
                                Register a URL scheme and universal / app link domains
  denext mobile add push        Push notifications (entitlement, AppDelegate, permission)
  denext mobile add auth-session --scheme myapp
                                OAuth in a system browser sheet (openAuthSession)
  denext mobile add share-extension --app-group group.com.example.app
                                Receive shared links, text and images (onShareReceived)
  denext mobile add widget --name Status
                                A home-screen widget fed by setWidgetData
  denext mobile add widget --name Usage --configurable period:enum=session|weekly
                                An iOS 17+ configurable widget (App Intents enum)
  denext mobile add live-activity --name Delivery
                                An iOS Live Activity (startLiveActivity)
  denext mobile add native-module --name Scanner
                                Your own Swift + Kotlin plugin (nativeModule, TurboModules)
  denext mobile add fastlane --ci
                                fastlane lanes (match, TestFlight, Play tracks) over
                                `mobile build`, a Gemfile, and a GitHub Actions workflow
  denext mobile add --list      List the capabilities and the plugins they install
  denext mobile add-ota [dir]   Install the DenextOta plugin into ios/ and android/
  denext mobile dev [project] --lan
                                Live reload on a device: point the app at `denext dev`
  denext mobile fingerprint --json > native.json
                                Hash the native layer (OTA-able vs needs a binary)
  denext mobile fingerprint --diff native.json
                                Explain which native inputs changed since native.json
  denext mobile fingerprint --write
                                Embed it in Info.plist + AndroidManifest (OTA gate)
  denext mobile privacy --check Validate ios/App/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy (--write merges
                                every installed capability's required-reason entries)
  denext mobile doctor --store  App Review readiness (server.url, usage strings, privacy
                                manifest, icons, account deletion, …); exits 1 on errors
  denext mobile doctor --release
                                Release security (debuggable WebView, cleartext, mixed
                                content, allowNavigation *, CSP, secrets in the export)
  denext mobile inspect         Attach Safari Web Inspector / chrome://inspect to the app
  denext mobile assets          Every icon and splash from assets/icon.png (+ splash.png)
  denext mobile assets --icon logo.png --background-color '#0f172a' --dark-background-color '#000'
                                Icons + splash, dark variants included
  denext mobile build android   Export, cap sync, gradle assembleDebug → dist/mobile/android/*.apk
  denext mobile build ios --release
                                Export, cap sync, xcodebuild archive + export → a signed .ipa
  denext mobile build ios --unsigned
                                An unsigned .ipa (CI without certificates)
  denext mobile build android --release --flavor staging
                                A signed .aab with the staging flavor's id, name and URL
  denext mobile build ios --dry-run
                                The plan: commands, signing, artifact (nothing runs)
  denext mobile submit ios --dry-run
                                Check the .ipa, the API key and the app in App Store Connect
  denext mobile submit android --track internal
                                Upload the newest .aab to Google Play's internal track

  fingerprint: SHA-256 over the ios/ and android/ sources (minus build output, Pods,
  .gradle, xcuserdata, local.properties and what `cap sync` copies in; text with CRLF
  normalised), capacitor.config.* without its server block, and the installed versions of
  @capacitor/* and every Capacitor / Cordova plugin package.json declares. The same
  fingerprint means the change can ship over the air; a different one needs a new binary.
  --write stores it as Info.plist DenextNativeFingerprint and the
  dev.denext.native.FINGERPRINT meta-data (never changing the value itself); a manifest
  stamped with `denext ota manifest --native-fingerprint` is then refused by a binary with
  another one (code native_mismatch).

  dev: starts `denext dev` for [project] (default: .) on --port (default 3000), or attaches
  to a server already answering there; writes server: { url, cleartext: true } into the
  Capacitor project's capacitor.config.* (--dir, else the current directory) and runs
  `npx cap copy`, so the app loads the dev server and reloads on every edit. --lan binds
  the LAN IPv4 (a physical device on the same network); without it the URL is
  localhost (the iOS simulator, or Android behind `adb reverse`). On iOS it also adds
  NSAppTransportSecurity > NSAllowsLocalNetworking and (when absent) an
  NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription to ios/App/App/Info.plist, without which the WebView
  never reaches a LAN server; a changed Info.plist needs a rebuild from Xcode. The edits
  are temporary: Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or an error puts the original bytes back and runs
  `cap copy` again. A killed run leaves a backup in .denext/; the next `mobile dev`, or
  `mobile dev --restore`, restores it first. The restore also takes the dev URL out of
  the native config copies itself, so they are clean even when `cap copy` fails because
  the webDir was never built (export and `npx cap copy` before a release build).

  add: finds the Capacitor project (the folder with capacitor.config.*: --dir when given,
  with no fallback, else the current directory), refuses when its @capacitor/core major
  is not the one the pinned plugins target, adds the packages with the package manager
  the nearest lockfile names (pnpm, npm, bun or yarn, looking up to the repository root
  for a workspace's; else a packageManager field; else npm) as caret ranges, or as exact
  versions (the range's minimum) when package.json pins every @capacitor/* package
  exactly, adds any Info.plist keys (never replacing yours) and Android permissions the
  capability needs, and runs `npx cap sync`. When the web export (capacitor.config webDir)
  has no index.html yet it runs `npx cap update` instead (the native half of sync, which
  cannot fail on the missing folder) and says to run `denext export`, then `npx cap sync`.
  --dry-run prints the plan and changes nothing. Ship a new app binary afterwards.

  deep-links takes --scheme (CFBundleURLTypes + a VIEW intent filter) and --domain
  (applinks: in the entitlements + an autoVerify https intent filter); give several as
  a comma-separated list. The domains must also serve apple-app-site-association and
  assetlinks.json. push writes aps-environment (development) into the entitlements, the
  token forwarding into AppDelegate.swift and POST_NOTIFICATIONS into the manifest, and
  warns when android/app/google-services.json (FCM) is missing. A new entitlements file
  (ios/App/App/App.entitlements) must be selected in Xcode (Code Signing Entitlements);
  the steps left to do by hand are printed.

  auth-session has no npm package: it writes denext's DenextAuthSession plugin
  (ios/App/App/DenextAuthSessionPlugin.swift, an ASWebAuthenticationSession sheet, added to
  the App target; android dev/denext/authsession/*.java, a Custom Tab) and registers it
  through DenextBridgeViewController and MainActivity, which it shares with add-ota (either
  order works). --scheme registers the OAuth callback scheme as deep-links does; Android
  needs it to receive the redirect. No install or `cap sync` runs for it alone.

  back (Android) adds @capacitor/app, denext's DenextBack plugin (predictive-back progress
  for onBack / useBackProgress) registered in MainActivity, and
  android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" on <application>. system-bars has no npm
  package (SystemBars ships in @capacitor/core 8): it sets
  UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance in Info.plist and calls EdgeToEdge.enable(this)
  in MainActivity. keyboard adds @capacitor/keyboard for useKeyboard and the keyboard views.
  dialog adds @capacitor/dialog, so React Native mode's Alert.alert / Alert.prompt show
  system dialogs.

  accessibility has no npm package: it writes denext's DenextAccessibility plugin
  (VoiceOver / TalkBack state for isScreenReaderEnabled, and React Native mode's
  AccessibilityInfo), registered like auth-session. background-location adds
  @capgo/background-geolocation, UIBackgroundModes location,
  NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription and Android's FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION
  (not ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION), and prints the App Store and Play review steps.
  application adds @capacitor/app and @capacitor/device (expo-application). camera also
  adds NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (video recorded in the page has sound).

  context-menu has no npm package: it writes denext's DenextContextMenu plugin (the
  UIContextMenuInteraction long-press menu with its lifted preview and UIMenu on iOS, a
  PopupMenu on Android) behind showContextMenu / useContextMenu. system-icons writes the
  DenextSystemIcon plugin (iOS only) that renders SF Symbols for <SystemIcon>.

  share-extension, widget and live-activity add app extensions (no npm package either).
  share-extension: an iOS Share Extension target (ios/App/DenextShareExtension, embedded in
  the app) that queues shares in the App Group container and opens the app with its URL
  scheme (--scheme, else the app's first CFBundleURLSchemes entry), and Android SEND /
  SEND_MULTIPLE intent filters. widget --name <Name>: a WidgetKit extension target
  (ios/App/DenextWidgets) with <Name>Widget.swift, and an Android AppWidgetProvider with its
  layout and manifest receiver. --configurable <param:enum=a|b,...> makes it configurable on
  iOS 17+ (an App Intents enum per parameter; static on 14-16 and on Android), and
  setWidgetData(kind, data, { params }) stores the snapshot for the chosen values.
  live-activity --name <Name> (iOS 16.1+, the app keeps its
  deployment target): an ActivityKit UI in the same extension and NSSupportsLiveActivities.
  Each writes a denext plugin into the app, and the App Group (--app-group, default
  group.<bundle id>) into the app's and the extension's entitlements; the group must exist
  in the Apple Developer portal (automatic signing usually registers it). Several names are
  comma-separated. The widget and Live Activity views are yours to edit: an edited file is
  kept on the next run.

  fastlane is release tooling for teams that already use fastlane (`mobile build` and
  `mobile submit` need none of it): it writes fastlane/Appfile (capacitor.config appId; the
  team and Play key from the environment), fastlane/Fastfile (ios and android build, beta
  and release lanes that run `denext mobile build <platform> --release` and hand its
  artifact to match, upload_to_testflight / upload_to_app_store and upload_to_play_store;
  flavor:, build_number:, bump: and track: pass through), fastlane/Matchfile, a
  fastlane/.gitignore and a Gemfile pinning fastlane. --ci also writes
  .github/workflows/mobile-release.yml at the repository root (ruby/setup-ruby, then
  `bundle exec fastlane <platform> <lane>`, credentials as repository secrets). Edited files
  are kept on a re-run (--force replaces them); nothing is installed and no `cap sync` runs.

  iOS: writes DenextOtaPlugin.swift, DenextOtaStore.swift and DenextBridgeViewController.swift
  into ios/App/App/, adds them to the App target in project.pbxproj, and switches
  Main.storyboard and SceneDelegate to DenextBridgeViewController when they still use
  CAPBridgeViewController. Android: writes dev/denext/ota/*.java and calls
  DenextOta.prepare(this, bridgeBuilder) from MainActivity, when it is the stock one or one
  denext generated (recognised by its marker line, or as a shape an earlier denext shipped).
  Customised files are left alone and listed as one-line manual steps, as are a MainActivity
  or bridge view controller a newer denext wrote (never downgraded). Safe to run again, and
  run it after every denext upgrade: unedited templates from an earlier denext are upgraded
  in place (ship a new app binary afterwards).

  --public-key ota.key.pub (from `denext ota keygen`) embeds the verifying key as Info.plist
  DenextOtaPublicKey and the dev.denext.ota.PUBLIC_KEY meta-data in AndroidManifest.xml
  (replacing an earlier one); the app then refuses any manifest not signed with its key.
  It exits non-zero when the key cannot be embedded on an installed platform, or an edited
  template was kept. --dry-run lists what it would write, upgrade or keep and changes
  nothing.

  privacy: prints ios/App/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy and validates it against Apple's
  required-reason categories and codes, the collected-data values, the entries the
  installed capabilities need (`mobile add` merges them; --write merges them now, never
  removing an entry) and whether Xcode copies it into the app. --check exits 1 on an error.

  doctor: --store checks what App Review looks at (a leftover server.url, cleartext / ATS
  exceptions, a debuggable WebView, usage strings for installed plugins, the privacy
  manifest, icons and splash, allowNavigation *, the CSP, source maps and secrets in the
  export, account deletion when the app signs users in). --release checks the release
  security settings (debuggable WebView, cleartext, mixed content, allowNavigation *,
  android:debuggable, the CSP, secrets in the export). Both read the native config copies
  `cap sync` wrote (what ships) as well as capacitor.config.*; run them after export + sync.
  With a fastlane/ folder, --release also checks it: the Appfile ids against capacitor.config,
  a Gemfile with its lock, a Fastfile that skips `denext export` + `cap sync`, and secrets in
  or written into fastlane/.

  inspect: prints how to attach Safari's Web Inspector (iOS) and chrome://inspect (Android)
  to the app's WebView, opens Safari (macOS) and Chrome at chrome://inspect/#devices, and
  lists `adb devices`, best effort. `mobile dev` turns WebView debugging on for its session
  only.

  assets: writes the iOS app icon (1024², RGB: App Store Connect refuses an alpha channel)
  and its iOS 18 dark variant, the iOS splash set, Android's legacy, round, adaptive
  (foreground + background colour) and themed (monochrome) launcher icons for every density,
  and the portrait / landscape splash drawables; the dark splash variants (asset catalog
  appearances, drawable-night) when --splash-dark or --dark-background-color is given.
  Sources default to assets/ (or resources/): icon.png, icon-foreground.png, icon-dark.png,
  splash.png, splash-dark.png. Decoding and resizing run on @denext/photon (wasm).

  build: `denext export` (--app, default the Capacitor project; a flavor's env is added),
  the flavor's edits, `npx cap sync <platform>`, then the native build. Without --release:
  a Debug build (Android: a debug-signed .apk). iOS signs automatically (-allowProvisioning
  Updates) for --team / DENEXT_IOS_TEAM, with DENEXT_ASC_KEY_PATH / _KEY_ID / _ISSUER_ID as the
  API key on a machine with no Apple ID signed in; --unsigned needs no certificate. Android
  --release signs with DENEXT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE, DENEXT_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS,
  DENEXT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD and DENEXT_ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD, passed to Gradle through
  the environment (never argv, never printed). --build-number / --version-name apply to this
  build only; --bump increments the build number in the sources. Flavors
  (denext.config mobile.flavors) change the app id, name, server.url and icons for the build
  and are restored afterwards; a killed build is restored by the next one or by
  `mobile build --restore`. The artifact and a <artifact>.json sidecar land in
  dist/mobile/<platform>[-<flavor>]/.

  submit: checks the artifact (signed, well formed) and the credentials, then uploads: iOS
  with `xcrun altool --upload-app` and the App Store Connect API key, Android through the
  Google Play Developer API with a service account (edit → upload → track → commit).
  --dry-run uploads nothing: it signs a token with the key and, unless --offline, looks the
  app up (App Store Connect) or opens and deletes an edit (Play). Exits 1 on a failed check.
```

- `action` required — add | add-ota | dev | fingerprint | privacy | doctor | inspect | assets | build | submit
- `args` optional — add: capability names (see --list); add-ota, fingerprint, privacy, doctor, inspect: the Capacitor project (default: .); dev: the denext project (default: .); build, submit: ios or android

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force` | boolean | Replace native template files that differ from denext's (loses local edits; add-ota, add auth-session / share-extension / widget / live-activity / native-module / fastlane) |
| `--public-key <file>` | string | Embed this OTA public key (base64 SPKI or PUBLIC KEY PEM) so the app verifies signatures |
| `--ota-origin <origin>` | string | add-ota: pin an https origin the app takes UI updates from; the only one unsigned updates come from (repeatable, or comma-separated) |
| `--dir <dir>` | string | add, dev, fingerprint, privacy, doctor, inspect, assets, build, submit: the Capacitor project, with no fallback (default: the current directory) |
| `--diff <old.json>` | string | fingerprint: explain which inputs changed since an earlier `fingerprint --json` |
| `--write` | boolean | fingerprint: embed it in Info.plist (DenextNativeFingerprint) and AndroidManifest (dev.denext.native.FINGERPRINT); privacy: merge every installed capability's entries into PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy |
| `--check` | boolean | privacy: exit 1 when the privacy manifest has an error (a CI gate) |
| `--store` | boolean | doctor: App Review readiness checks (exit 1 on an error) |
| `--release` | boolean | doctor: release security checks (exit 1 on an error); build: a Release build (.ipa, .aab) |
| `--app <dir>` | string | doctor: the denext app scanned for sign-in and account deletion; build: the denext app to export (default: the Capacitor project) |
| `--platform <ios\|android>` | string | inspect: one platform's steps; assets: one platform's files (default: both) |
| `--lan` | boolean | dev: serve on the LAN IPv4 so a physical device on the network can load it |
| `--port, -p <port>` | number | dev: the dev server port (default: 3000) |
| `--host <host>` | string | dev: the host to bind and load (default: localhost; --lan picks the LAN IPv4) |
| `--restore` | boolean | dev: only put back what an interrupted session left (capacitor.config, Info.plist, the dev URL in the native config copies), then run `cap copy`; build: put back what an interrupted build's flavor edits left |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | add, add-ota, privacy --write, assets, build: print the plan (packages, native files, config, commands) and change nothing; inspect: print the steps without opening anything; submit: check everything, upload nothing |
| `--list` | boolean | add: list the capabilities and the plugins they install |
| `--ci` | boolean | add fastlane: also write .github/workflows/mobile-release.yml (fastlane in GitHub Actions) |
| `--scheme <scheme[,scheme]>` | string | add deep-links / auth-session / share-extension: custom URL schemes to register (comma-separated) |
| `--domain <host[,host]>` | string | add deep-links: universal link / app link domains (comma-separated) |
| `--app-group <group>` | string | add share-extension / widget / live-activity: the App Group shared with the extension (default: group.<bundle id>) |
| `--name <Name[,Name]>` | string | add widget / live-activity / native-module: PascalCase names (comma-separated) |
| `--configurable <param:enum=a\|b[,…]>` | string | add widget: iOS 17+ configurable widget with these enum parameters (the first value is the default; re-runs keep them) |
| `--icon <png>` | string | assets: the app icon (default: assets/icon.png) |
| `--icon-foreground <png>` | string | assets: Android's adaptive foreground layer (default: assets/icon-foreground.png, else the icon) |
| `--icon-dark <png>` | string | assets: the iOS 18 dark icon (default: assets/icon-dark.png) |
| `--splash <png>` | string | assets: the splash (default: assets/splash.png, else the icon on the background) |
| `--splash-dark <png>` | string | assets: the dark splash (default: assets/splash-dark.png) |
| `--background-color <#hex>` | string | assets: icon and splash background (default: #ffffff) |
| `--dark-background-color <#hex>` | string | assets: the dark splash background (writes the dark variants) |
| `--flavor <name>` | string | build, submit: a flavor from denext.config mobile.flavors |
| `--unsigned` | boolean | build ios: archive without signing (an unsigned .ipa for CI) |
| `--apk` | boolean | build android --release: an .apk instead of an .aab |
| `--build-number <n>` | number | build: the build number for this build only |
| `--version-name <x.y.z>` | string | build: the version for this build only |
| `--bump` | boolean | build: increment the build number in the native sources first (commit it) |
| `--skip-export` | boolean | build: skip `denext export` (the web export is already there) |
| `--jobs <n>` | number | build: parallel jobs (xcodebuild -jobs, gradle --max-workers) |
| `--team <id>` | string | build ios: the Apple team id (default: $DENEXT_IOS_TEAM, else the project's) |
| `--asc-key <p8>` | string | build, submit ios: App Store Connect API key file (default: $DENEXT_ASC_KEY_PATH) |
| `--asc-key-id <id>` | string | build, submit ios: its key id (default: $DENEXT_ASC_KEY_ID, or AuthKey_<id>.p8) |
| `--asc-issuer <id>` | string | build, submit ios: its issuer id (default: $DENEXT_ASC_ISSUER_ID) |
| `--export-method <method>` | string | build ios: app-store-connect (--release default), release-testing, debugging, enterprise |
| `--export-options <plist>` | string | build ios: your own ExportOptions.plist |
| `--keystore <jks>` | string | build android --release: the upload keystore (default: $DENEXT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE) |
| `--key-alias <alias>` | string | build android: the key alias (default: $DENEXT_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS) |
| `--out <dir>` | string | build, submit: the artifact directory (default: dist/mobile) |
| `--file <ipa\|aab\|apk>` | string | submit: the artifact (default: the newest build) |
| `--app-id <id>` | string | submit: the bundle id / package name (default: the build's) |
| `--service-account <json>` | string | submit android: the Play service-account key (default: $DENEXT_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT) |
| `--track <track>` | string | submit android: the release track (default: internal) |
| `--draft` | boolean | submit android: leave the release as a draft |
| `--offline` | boolean | submit --dry-run: skip the network checks |

chunks.title: `denext ota`
chunks.text:
## `denext ota`

Over-the-air UI manifest for Capacitor apps

```sh
denext ota <action> [path] [options]

  denext ota manifest out     Write out/_denext/ota.json (paths, SHA-256s, sizes, version)
  denext ota manifest out --required --notes "Fixes sign-in"
                              Also mark the UI required and attach release notes
  denext ota manifest out --sign ota.key
                              Also sign it (or set DENEXT_OTA_SIGNING_KEY to the PEM);
                              signing stamps --sequence (default: the Unix time) so apps
                              refuse an older release, and --min-native <build> refuses
                              app binaries older than that build number
  denext ota manifest out --native-fingerprint auto --dir .
                              Also stamp the native fingerprint of the Capacitor project at
                              --dir; a binary embedding another one (`denext mobile
                              fingerprint --write`) refuses it (code native_mismatch)
  denext ota manifest out --platform ios
                              Name the target the export was built for (`denext export
                              --platform ios` stamps it already); a shell of another target
                              refuses it (code platform_mismatch)
  denext ota keygen ota.key   Write a P-256 signing key (0600) and ota.key.pub
  denext ota channel beta releases/2026-09-27
                              Point channel beta at an export (ota-channels.json, --file)
  denext ota promote --channel beta --to production --percent 20
                              Roll beta's release out to 20% of production's devices
  denext ota promote --channel beta --to production
                              Make it production's release (100%; ends the rollout)
  denext ota promote --to production --halt
                              Stop production's rollout; its stable release stays

  Run it after anything that changes the export (e.g. swapping brand icons in), and before
  `cap sync`, so the bundled UI and the served UI carry the right version. `spa.ota: true`
  makes `denext export` write it for you. `*.gz` files are never listed. `--required` and
  `--notes` feed the app's own update prompt (prepareUiUpdate in denext/mobile); they are
  not part of the version, but the signature covers them. An app whose binary embeds the
  public key (`denext mobile add-ota --public-key ota.key.pub`) refuses an unsigned or
  wrongly signed manifest; one without a key refuses plain http beyond loopback. Signing
  protects integrity only: over plain http the headers (bearer tokens) are visible on the
  network. `keygen --force` rotates the key, which breaks OTA for every installed binary
  that embeds the old public key.
```

- `action` required — manifest | keygen | channel | promote
- `path` optional — manifest: the static export directory (e.g. out); keygen: the private key file; channel: <name> <dir>

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--required` | boolean | Mark this UI as a required update (the app should not let users decline it) |
| `--notes <text>` | string | Release notes for the app's update prompt (at most 2000 characters) |
| `--sign <keyfile>` | string | Sign the manifest with this PKCS#8 PEM key (default: $DENEXT_OTA_SIGNING_KEY, if set) |
| `--sequence <n>` | number | Release sequence (a non-negative integer that only grows; default when signing: the Unix time in seconds) |
| `--min-native <build>` | number | Refuse this UI on app binaries whose build number (CFBundleVersion / versionCode) is lower |
| `--native-fingerprint <fp\|auto>` | string | Stamp the native fingerprint this UI was built for (auto: compute it for --dir); binaries embedding another refuse it |
| `--platform <target>` | string | manifest: the target the export was built for (ios, android, macos, windows, linux, web); shells of another target refuse it |
| `--dir <dir>` | string | manifest --native-fingerprint auto: the Capacitor project (default: the current directory) |
| `--force` | boolean | keygen: replace existing key files (breaks OTA for binaries that embed the old public key); channel / promote: skip the signature and sequence checks |
| `--channel <name>` | string | promote: the source channel (its stable release is promoted) |
| `--release <dir>` | string | promote: the source export directory (instead of --channel) |
| `--to <name>` | string | promote: the target channel |
| `--percent <n>` | number | promote: the share of devices that get it (default 100 = the stable release; 0 halts) |
| `--halt` | boolean | promote: stop the target channel's staged rollout (its stable release stays) |
| `--file <file>` | string | promote, channel: the channels file (default: ota-channels.json) |

chunks.title: `denext patch`
chunks.text:
## `denext patch`

Patch npm packages — or denext itself (patches/*.patch)

```sh
denext patch <action> [name] [file] [dir]

  denext patch create <package|denext> [dir]
  denext patch list [dir]
  denext patch delete <name|index> [dir]
  denext patch apply [dir]
  denext patch edit <package|denext> <file> [dir]

  create  diff the package's installed files (node_modules/<pkg>) — or denext's working
          copies (patches/.work/denext/) — against pristine → patches/<name>+<version>.patch
          (added and deleted files are recorded; a file over 2 MiB / 50k lines is skipped)
  list    the patches, indexed
  delete  remove a patch and undo it (npm files reverted, denext mapping dropped)
  apply   apply every patch now (dev/build/start/export do this at boot)
  edit    for denext: copy a framework file to patches/.work/denext/ to edit;
          for a package: print the installed file's path

  denext patch edit denext src/server/document.ts
  denext patch create denext
  denext patch create left-pad
  denext patch delete 2
```

- `action` required — create | list | delete | apply | edit
- `name` optional — Package name, `denext`, or (delete) a list index
- `file` optional — (edit) path inside the package
- `dir` optional — Project directory (default: .)

No flags.

chunks.title: `denext plugin`
chunks.text:
## `denext plugin`

Manage denext plugins (add, remove, list)

```sh
denext plugin <action> [pkg] [dir] [options]

  denext plugin add <pkg> [dir]
  denext plugin remove <pkg> [dir]
  denext plugin list [dir]

  add     adds the dependency (deno add) and wires the plugin into denext.config.ts
  remove  unwires the plugin from denext.config.ts and drops the dependency
  list    show the plugins wired into denext.config.ts

  denext plugin add @denext/htmx
  denext plugin remove @denext/htmx
  denext plugin list
  denext plugin add my-plugin --export configureMyPlugin
```

- `action` required — add | remove | list
- `pkg` optional — Plugin package for add/remove (e.g. @denext/htmx)
- `dir` optional — Project directory (default: .)

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--export <name>` | string | Factory export name (default: camelCased package name) |
| `--no-call` | boolean | Plugin is a ready value, not a factory — omit () |

chunks.title: `denext test`
chunks.text:
## `denext test`

Run the app's tests (deno test)

```sh
denext test [paths] [-- <deno args>]

Forwards to `deno test -A`. Extra args/paths pass through:
  denext test                  Run every test
  denext test --watch          Re-run on change (deno test --watch)
  denext test --coverage=cov   Collect coverage, then `deno coverage cov`

```

chunks.title: `denext ui`
chunks.text:
## `denext ui`

Open the project management UI in a browser (loopback only)

```sh
denext ui [dir] [options]

  denext ui                    Serve the UI for the current project and open it
  denext ui ./my-app --port 6000   That exact port, or a clear error if it is taken
  denext ui --read-only        Browse without offering any write
  denext ui --offline          Keep the UI and the processes it starts off the network
  denext ui --no-open --json   Print { url, port, token } and keep serving

  The UI binds and is opened at 127.0.0.1 only (never localhost, whose cookies every
  local server shares). The printed URL carries a per-launch 256-bit token that is
  exchanged ONCE for an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie holding a separate, freshly
  minted secret — the query token is then refused, so a copied link cannot open a
  second session. Every mutation additionally needs a same-origin Origin and a CSRF
  token derived from the cookie.
  Note: with --open, the token is visible in the browser-launcher's argv on this machine.
```

- `dir` optional — Project directory (default: .)

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--port <port>` | number | Port to listen on (default 5177, which falls forward when busy; an explicit --port is required exactly, and 0 picks a free one) |
| `--no-open` | boolean | Don't launch a browser |
| `--read-only` | boolean | Refuse every mutation |
| `--offline` | boolean | Never reach the network: no JSR search; denext verbs and doctor run with --deny-net --cached-only, deno install with --cached-only; deno task, denext dev and plugin add/remove are refused (combines with --read-only) |
| `--token <token>` | string | Use this session token instead of minting one (at least 22 characters) |
| `--ui-dev` | boolean | Internal: watch src/ui and reload open pages on change |

chunks.title: `denext update`
chunks.text:
## `denext update`

Update dependencies to latest (deno outdated --update)

```sh
denext update [packages] [-- <deno args>]

Forwards to `deno outdated --update`. Pass package names to scope it,
or `--latest` to cross semver ranges.
```

- `packages` optional — Packages to update (default: all)

No flags.

Everything under `app/` is a Server Component until a file starts with
`"use client"`. That file and everything it imports ship to the browser; the
components it exports are the interactive leaves of the tree. This page is the
toolkit for those leaves. The rules of the boundary itself (what can cross it,
why a function prop cannot) are on [Islands & hydration](/docs/islands); the
lint rules that enforce hook placement are `denext/rules-of-hooks`,
`denext/hooks-in-component` and `denext/no-hooks-in-async`.

Every hook here is imported from **`denext`** (the React hooks are also on
`denext/client`; the utility hooks are on `denext` only). `createPortal` lives
on `denext/client`.

chunks.text:
denext is a web framework (Next.js's App Router on Deno) that also ships to phones: the app is
exported to static files and a [Capacitor](https://capacitorjs.com) shell runs it in the
system WebView. [`denext/mobile`](/docs/mobile) is the client runtime for that shell, and
`denext mobile` installs the native side. Components render to the DOM, not to native views.

There are two ways in:

- **New code, or a web app going mobile:** write a denext app and add the Capacitor shell.
  Start with the [Mobile quickstart](/docs/mobile#quickstart).
- **An existing Expo / React Native app:** `denext migrate --from expo` builds the app's own
  source for the web through react-native-web, with the `expo-*` packages resolved to denext
  shims. See [React Native / Expo apps](/docs/react-native#migrating-an-expo-app).

The table says which one each row is about.

chunks.title: Concept map
chunks.text:
## Concept map

| React Native / Expo                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | denext                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `package.json`, Metro config, `app.json`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `deno.json` (imports and tasks) and `denext.config.ts`; `capacitor.config.ts` for the shell                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | A `package.json` stays for the npm packages Capacitor and its plugins need. `denext migrate --from expo` writes all three files from the Expo app.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Prebuild, config plugins                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | The committed `ios/` and `android/` projects, and the `denext mobile add` generators                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Capacitor projects are not regenerated: you commit them and edit them. `denext mobile add` writes the Info.plist keys, entitlements, manifest entries and native files a capability needs.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `View`, `Text`, `Pressable`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | HTML elements (`div`, `p`, `button`) in new code; react-native-web's components in [React Native mode](/docs/react-native)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | React Native mode resolves `react-native` to react-native-web, so an Expo app's components run unchanged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `StyleSheet`, inline styles                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | CSS, CSS Modules or Tailwind ([Styling](/docs/styling)) in new code; react-native-web's `StyleSheet` in React Native mode                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | uniwind (Tailwind for React Native components) has a [recipe](/docs/react-native#recipe-uniwind-and-tailwind).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| React Navigation, expo-router                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The App Router (`app/` routes, `Link`, `useRouter`) in new code, with `StackLayout` / `TabsLayout` from `denext/navigation` ([Native-feel navigation](/docs/navigation-native)); expo-router in React Native mode                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | expo-router's routes are found at build time from `app/` ([expo-router](/docs/react-native#expo-router)). A client-only app can also use a history-based router in [SPA mode](/docs/spa).                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `@react-navigation/native-stack`, `bottom-tabs`, `drawer`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | In React Native mode `createNativeStackNavigator` / `createBottomTabNavigator` are drawn by `denext/navigation` (kept screens, platform animations, swipe back, sheets), and `createDrawerNavigator` by a denext drawer, all over React Navigation's routers                                                                                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Stack screens, native headers (`react-native-screens`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `StackLayout` from `denext/navigation`: kept screens, platform push/pop animations, the iOS swipe-back that follows the finger, Android predictive back, a native-style header, and `modal` / `formSheet` presentations ([Native-feel navigation](/docs/navigation-native))                                                                                                                                                       | Screens are DOM, not native views. In React Native mode, expo-router's `Stack` and `Tabs` are drawn by the same views.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Animated`, Reanimated                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | CSS transitions and animations, `ViewTransition` in new code. In React Native mode, react-native-web's `Animated` and Reanimated's web build run unchanged: the build stamps Reanimated's worklets, so hooks need no dependency arrays, but they run on the main thread; `transform` / `opacity` animations run on the compositor ([Reanimated](/docs/react-native#reanimated-and-worklets))                                      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| react-native-gesture-handler                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Pointer and touch events; `useBackSwipe(onBack)` from `denext/mobile`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Gesture handler's web build works in React Native mode with reduced features. There is no native gesture system.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `FlatList`, `SectionList`, `VirtualizedList`, FlashList, LegendList                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Unchanged in React Native mode: they run on denext's `VirtualList` (`reactNative.lists: "denext"`, the default). In new code, use `VirtualList` / `useVirtualList` from `denext` (and `VirtualMasonry` from `denext/virtual-masonry`).                                                                                                                                                                                            | Their props and ref methods carry over, including `inverted` (a logical reversal, not a transform), `getItemLayout`, `numColumns`, sections with sticky headers, `scrollToLocation` and viewability. `onScrollToIndexFailed` never fires because `scrollToIndex` is exact. `reactNative: { lists: "library" }` keeps the libraries' own engines. See [Lists & scrolling](/docs/lists#react-native). |
| `Platform.OS`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `runtimePlatform()` (`"ios"`, `"android"`, `"desktop"` or `"web"`) from `denext/mobile`. In React Native mode `Platform.OS` stays `"web"` (react-native-web and libraries pick their DOM paths by it), `Platform.select` picks the shell's `ios` / `android` key when there is no `web` key, and `Platform.constants.denextShell` tells the shells apart ([Platform.OS in the shell](/docs/react-native#platformos-in-the-shell)) |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Platform-specific extensions (`.ios.tsx`, `.android.tsx`, `.native.tsx`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | The same files resolve in each target's export (`denext mobile build ios` picks `.ios` → `.mobile` → `.web` → plain), plus `.macos` / `.windows` / `.linux` / `.desktop` for desktop packages ([Platform-specific files](/docs/platform-files))                                                                                                                                                                                   | `.native` is opt-in (`platformExtensions: { native: true }`): it usually holds native code. Packages keep their web build.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SafeAreaView`, react-native-safe-area-context                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `SAFE_AREA_CSS` and `viewport-fit=cover`; in React Native mode react-native-safe-area-context resolves to a provider, `SafeAreaView` and hooks over `useSafeAreaInsets` ([Community packages](/docs/react-native#community-packages))                                                                                                                                                                                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Keyboard`, `KeyboardAvoidingView`, react-native-keyboard-controller                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `useKeyboard()` / `onKeyboardChange`, `<KeyboardAvoidingView>` and `<KeyboardStickyView>` from `denext/mobile` (`denext mobile add keyboard`); in React Native mode react-native-keyboard-controller resolves to them, with `KeyboardAwareScrollView`, `KeyboardToolbar` and the handler hooks                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `BackHandler` (Android back button)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `onBack` / `useBackHandler` and `useBackProgress` for predictive back (`denext mobile add back`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | In React Native mode, `BackHandler.addEventListener("hardwareBackPress", …)` runs on that stack in the Android shell.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `StatusBar`, expo-status-bar                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `setSystemBars` / `useSystemBarsFollowTheme` over Capacitor 8's `SystemBars` (`denext mobile add system-bars`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | In React Native mode, `<StatusBar>` and its static methods, and expo-status-bar's `<StatusBar style="auto" />`, drive the system bars in the shell.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Alert.alert`, `Alert.prompt`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | System dialogs through `@capacitor/dialog` (`denext mobile add dialog`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | In React Native mode `Alert` shows the system dialog when it fits one (up to two buttons, a plain-text prompt), else an accessible in-page dialog; react-native-web's `Alert` does nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `RefreshControl` (pull-to-refresh)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `<PullToRefresh refreshing onRefresh>` from `denext/mobile`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | In React Native mode, `RefreshControl` on a `ScrollView` / `FlatList` is the same touch gesture and spinner.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `AppState` (returning to the foreground)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `useAppResume((awayMs) => …)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Reports how long the app was in the background.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Linking.openURL`, expo-web-browser                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `openExternal(url)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | The in-app browser with the `browser` capability installed, else `window.open`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Native modules, Expo modules, TurboModules                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Capacitor plugins: `denext mobile add <capability>` for the common ones, any Capacitor plugin from npm, or your own (`denext mobile add native-module`, called through `nativeModule`). In React Native mode `TurboModuleRegistry`, `NativeModules` and Expo's `requireNativeModule` reach your plugin by name ([Your own native code](/docs/native-code))                                                                        | A Capacitor plugin exposes an async JavaScript API over native Swift / Kotlin / Java. There is no true synchronous native call: `react-native-mmkv` keeps its sync API over an in-memory mirror (writes reach the durable store a moment later), and the sync `expo-sqlite` API and Nitro modules have no equivalent. See [Native capabilities](/docs/mobile#native-capabilities).                  |
| react-native-permissions, react-native-keychain, react-native-share, react-native-haptic-feedback, react-native-biometrics, react-native-bootsplash, @notifee/react-native, @react-native-community/netinfo, react-native-device-info, @react-native-google-signin/google-signin, react-native-purchases | Unchanged imports in React Native mode: each resolves to a stand-in over the matching `denext/mobile` API (`checkPermission`, `secureStore`, `share`, `haptic`, `authenticateBiometric`, `hideSplash`, local notifications, `networkStatus`, `deviceInfo`, `signInWithGoogle`, `purchases`) ([Community packages](/docs/react-native#community-packages))                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| react-native-webview, react-native-pager-view                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | An `<iframe>` with a `postMessage` bridge (injection only for inline HTML and same-origin pages; the frame runs in the app's WebView, so frame only content you trust); a CSS scroll-snap pager                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| react-native-maps, expo-maps, react-native-video, expo-video, expo-symbols                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Native views on a box in the page: `<NativeViewSlot type="map">` / `"video"` from `denext/mobile` (`denext mobile add native-map` / `native-views`), and `<SystemIcon>` (`denext mobile add system-icons`). In React Native mode these packages resolve to them                                                                                                                                                                   | On iOS a map is embedded in the page's scroll view and a video drawn under the page with AVKit's controls; on the web the maps show a placeholder and the video is an HTML `<video>`. See [Native views](/docs/mobile#native-views).                                                                                                                                                                |
| @react-native-async-storage/async-storage, react-native-mmkv                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Unchanged imports in React Native mode, over `openKeyValueStore` (a SQLite file with `denext mobile add storage`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Not the WebView's `localStorage`, which the OS may clear. See [Durable storage](/docs/react-native#durable-storage).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| @react-native-firebase/*, react-native-iap, @stripe/stripe-react-native                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The Firebase web SDK or Capacitor Firebase plugins, `sendPush`; RevenueCat (`denext mobile add purchases`) or a StoreKit / Play Billing plugin; Stripe.js or a Capacitor Stripe plugin                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Native-only, with no alias. See [Native SDK recipes](/docs/native-sdk-recipes).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
