chunks.title: Other native-only packages
chunks.text:
## Other native-only packages

Packages with no web build and no denext shim or alias (native modules, Nitro/JSI packages)
still need a web replacement of your own. A TurboModule / Fabric codegen package loads as it
is, because of the [codegen entry points](#what-reactnative-does): its spec's top-level
`getEnforcing` no longer throws, and a `requireNativeComponent` view renders its children
unless the view type is registered natively, so the package fails only when its native module
is actually used. It still needs a replacement if
the web build calls into that module, unless the app ships that module as a Capacitor plugin of
the same name ([Your own native code](/docs/native-code)). An Expo module that calls
`requireNativeModule` at the top level loads too: off-device the call returns a stand-in whose
functions throw `Cannot find native module` only when called. One kind fails earlier, before
any use: a package whose `main` is Flow source (a parse error at build time). The
listed [Expo shims](#expo-apis) and [community packages](#community-packages) cover the common
ones; `denext migrate --from expo` names the native-only packages it finds, and
[Native SDK recipes](/docs/native-sdk-recipes) covers the most used ones (Firebase, in-app
purchases, Stripe, file system, camera, config, crash reporting, CodePush). Two ways to replace
one:

- Add a `.web.ts` beside the module that imports it, exporting a web implementation. The
  platform-file rule picks it up.
- Map the package to a shim in `deno.json`'s `imports`, for example
  `"react-native-nitro-markdown": "./web-shims/nitro-markdown.ts"`.

chunks.title: Recipe: uniwind and Tailwind
chunks.text:
## Recipe: uniwind and Tailwind

uniwind styles React Native components with Tailwind classes. Its web
setup is specific to the app, so denext does not build it in. What it takes:

1. Compile the Tailwind input with denext's Tailwind integration:
   `tailwind: { input: "./global.css", output: "./global.gen.css" }` in `denext.config.ts`,
   and import `global.css` from the web entry.
2. Run `uniwind generate-artifacts` once for any themes beyond the default, and commit the
   generated CSS it writes.
3. Two importer-sensitive aliases: `react-native` imported from anywhere except uniwind's own
   files resolves to uniwind's web components (`uniwind/dist/module/components/web/index.js`),
   and react-native-web's `StyleSheet` importing `./createOrderedCSSStyleSheet` gets uniwind's
   version from the same directory.

denext's config has no seam for importer-sensitive aliases yet. Until it has one, apply step 3
with [`denext patch`](/docs/patches): patch `src/build/react-native.ts` so the `react-native`
resolver returns uniwind's index when the importer is outside `/uniwind/dist/`, and
`src/build/next-compat.ts`'s app resolver so the `./createOrderedCSSStyleSheet` import from
`react-native-web/dist/exports/StyleSheet` returns uniwind's file.

chunks.title: Recipe: NativeWind v4
chunks.text:
## Recipe: NativeWind v4

NativeWind v4 styles React Native components with Tailwind classes through
`react-native-css-interop`. With `nativewind` installed, React Native mode runs the app's own
JSX through `nativewind/jsx-runtime` (what NativeWind's Babel preset does with
`jsxImportSource: "nativewind"`), so `className` on a `View` or `Text` becomes class names
react-native-web renders. Packages keep the plain runtime. The Tailwind CSS is compiled by
Tailwind 3's CLI (NativeWind v4 targets Tailwind 3), the step NativeWind's Metro plugin runs:

1. Install `nativewind` and `tailwindcss@3`, and keep NativeWind's `tailwind.config.js` (its
   `presets: [require("nativewind/preset")]` and `content` globs) and `global.css`
   (`@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;`).
2. Compile it: `npx tailwindcss -i global.css -o src/nativewind.css` (add `--watch` beside
   `denext dev`, or run it from a `deno.json` task before `denext build`).
3. Import the output once from the web entry or the root component:
   `import "./nativewind.css";`.

`metro.config.js`'s `withNativeWind` and `babel.config.js`'s `nativewind/babel` are not used.
`reactNative: { aliases: { nativewind: false } }` turns the JSX runtime off.

chunks.title: Setup
How it works
chunks.text:
## How it works

React Router v7's framework mode is Remix's successor: routes are declared in `app/routes.ts` with `route()` / `index()` / `layout()` / `prefix()`, each route module exports a `loader`/`action` and a component, and `app/root.tsx` is the document shell. The plugin runs such an app on denext without touching its source:

- It evaluates `app/routes.ts` (the config DSL, imported from `@react-router/dev/routes` — aliased to `@denext/react-router/routes`).
- It generates a denext route module for each route under `.denext/react-router/`: the `"use client"` component split from its server `loader`/`action` data module, wrapped for the `denext/remix` runtime.
- It adds those routes through denext's **route-synthesizer** plugin seam, so Flight, streaming SSR, per-segment error boundaries, soft navigation, ISR and Fast Refresh are denext's own.

Loaders and actions, `meta`, `links`, `ErrorBoundary` (with `useRouteError`/`isRouteErrorResponse`), the root `Layout` export, and the `Route.ComponentProps` props contract (`loaderData`/`actionData`/`params`/`matches` as component props) all work — the framework API is Remix's, which denext already implements.

> Commit `.denext/react-router/`? No — it is generated on every build and dev scan (and gitignored with the rest of `.denext/`). Your `app/` files are the source of truth.

chunks.title: Limitations
chunks.text:
## Limitations

- **Server rendering only.** `clientLoader`, `clientAction` and `HydrateFallback` are not run — loaders and actions run on the server.
- `react-router.config.ts` `ssr: false` (RR's SPA mode) is not this plugin — use denext's `mode: "spa"` for a pure client app; `prerender` is not applied (denext prerenders static routes itself).
- Route typegen (`import type { Route } from "./+types/…"`) is type-only and erases at runtime, so the app runs without it.

denext supports the whole App Router rendering spectrum, and adds a second axis of fine-grained hydration that Next.js doesn't have. Two axes:

- **Parity** — SSR, SSG/static, ISR, CSR/SPA, **Streaming** (on by default, CSP-carrying, Flight-capable), and **PPR / Cache Components** (a cached shell + per-request holes, now Flight-capable).
- **Leadership** — directive-based **islands**, progressive **lazy hydration**, and **resumability** (zero up-front hydration).

chunks.title: Parity axis
chunks.text: ## Parity axis

chunks.title: SSR — dynamic, per request
SSG / static
ISR — incremental static regeneration
chunks.text:
### ISR — incremental static regeneration

Time- and tag-based regeneration with stale-while-revalidate, backed by real cache stores. See [Data & caching](/docs/data).

```tsx
export const revalidate = 10; // regenerate at most every 10s
```

chunks.title: CSR / SPA
chunks.text:
### CSR / SPA

Two routes to the client: whole-app [SPA mode](/docs/spa) (`mode: "spa"`, no SSR/Flight), or `"use client"` islands inside the App Router.

chunks.title: Streaming SSR — on by default
chunks.text:
### Streaming SSR — on by default

A route with pending `<Suspense>` boundaries streams: the shell and fallbacks flush first, then each boundary's real content streams in as a `<template>` revealed by a single hashed swap-runtime script. A route with no holes buffers (so it stays cache-friendly). Streaming carries the same strict **hash-based CSP** as a buffered response, and works on `"use client"` (Flight) routes.

```ts
// denext.config.ts — opt out if you need fully-buffered responses
export default { streaming: false };
```

**Inside a streamed boundary, the headers are already gone.** Once the shell has flushed, a component that resolves later inside a `<Suspense>` hole can no longer change the status line or the response headers. denext follows Next here — the same rules apply to a PPR hole and a Flight-route hole:

- `after(cb)` runs when the **stream ends** (after the last hole settled, or the stream was aborted), not when the Response object was created — so an `after()` registered inside a hole still runs, once.
- `redirect()` / `permanentRedirect()` become a **client-side redirect** streamed into the hole: a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` (honoured by browsers when the swap runtime inserts it) and nothing else in the hole. The destination goes through the same sanitiser as an HTTP `Location`. The response stays a 200. A *soft* navigation is never streamed, so there it is a real HTTP redirect as before.
- `notFound()` / `forbidden()` / `unauthorized()` reveal the **nearest boundary's UI** in place of the hole — the segment's `not-found.tsx` (…) or the built-in page — with the status left at 200, as in Next. Put the boundary *above* the `<Suspense>` if you need the 404 status itself.
- `cookies().set()` / `.delete()` cannot reach the response: in dev they throw ("cookies can only be modified before the response starts …"); in production the write is logged once per request and ignored. Set cookies in middleware, a Server Action, a Route Handler, or a component that renders in the shell.

The common `const session = (await auth()) ?? redirect("/login")` inside a Suspense'd component therefore works as expected: the visitor lands on `/login`, they just get there via the streamed tail.

chunks.title: PPR / Cache Components
chunks.text:
### PPR / Cache Components

With `cacheComponents: true` (a top-level config field), a cacheable page renders a request-independent **static shell** (cached once) with dynamic subtrees behind `<Suspense>` as **per-request holes**. A postpone-aware dual HTML+Flight renderer means this now works on routes with a `"use client"` boundary too — islands in the cached shell and inside resumed holes both hydrate.

> Cache Components / PPR is a stable **opt-in** — off unless you set `cacheComponents: true` (the legacy `experimental.cacheComponents` still works and warns in dev). Its documented bounds live in KNOWN-LIMITATIONS. Streaming, SSR, SSG, ISR, and CSR are on by default.

chunks.title: Route segment config
chunks.text:
### Route segment config

These exports are honored:

| Export | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `dynamic: "error"` | Throws if a dynamic API (cookies/headers/connection) is read. |
| `dynamic: "force-static"` | Dynamic APIs return empty and the page caches (no silent no-cache conflict). |
| `dynamicParams: false` | Params outside `generateStaticParams` 404. |
| `revalidate` / `fetchCache` | ISR timing; segment-level fetch-cache default. |
| `runtime` / `preferredRegion` / `maxDuration` | Informational — one Deno runtime, so no separate edge/region. |

chunks.title: Leadership axis — islands, lazy hydration, resumability
chunks.text:
## Leadership axis — islands, lazy hydration, resumability

denext ships fine-grained hydration Next.js doesn't have. A `client:*` directive turns a `"use client"` component into an **island** that hydrates on its own schedule instead of eagerly with the page — full 6/6 Astro directive parity, plus resumability Astro lacks. See the [Islands & hydration](/docs/islands) guide for the full per-directive reference.

chunks.title: The six island directives
chunks.text:
### The six island directives

| Directive | Hydrates when… |
| --- | --- |
| `client:load` | Immediately, but per-island (parity with eager). |
| `client:idle` | The main thread is idle (`requestIdleCallback`). |
| `client:visible` | The island scrolls into view (`IntersectionObserver`). |
| `client:interaction` | The first interaction inside it (the event is replayed). |
| `client:media="(min-width:800px)"` | A CSS media query matches (`matchMedia`). |
| `client:only` | On the client only — no SSR (no first paint; SEO/CLS tradeoff). |

```tsx
import Counter from "./Counter.tsx"; // a "use client" island

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <>
      <Counter client:visible />
      <Chart client:media="(min-width: 800px)" />
      <Cart client:idle />
    </>
  );
}
```

A module can set its own default with `export const hydrate = "visible"`; a usage-site `client:*` overrides it. Precedence: *usage-site > module default > eager*.

chunks.title: Resumability
chunks.text:
### Resumability

`export const resumable = true` makes a route interactive with **no up-front hydration** — plain state + event-handler components work unchanged, and only the touched island resumes. See [Resumability](/docs/resumability) for `qrl()` and reactive serializable signals.

> Islands and resumability run on the Flight (RSC) path — a route with a `"use client"` boundary or `resumable`. A `client:*` directive on an island nested inside another island defers independently — the inner island carves its own boundary rather than hydrating with its parent.

chunks.title: Async transitions & concurrency
What it is
chunks.text:
## What it is

There are two ways to make server-rendered HTML interactive in the browser:

- **Hydration** (React, Next.js). On load, the client re-executes the whole component tree to rebuild state and attach event handlers over the existing DOM. The cost scales with how much interactive UI the page has — and it is paid up front, whether or not the visitor ever touches any of it.
- **Resumption** (denext). The client attaches nothing on load. It adopts the server DOM as-is and runs a component only when that part of the page is first used — then replays the triggering event to the now-live handler. Time-to-interactive stays flat no matter how large the page grows.

> Resumability is not a denext invention — **Qwik** pioneered it (with related prior art in **Marko**). denext's contribution is running it behind the ordinary **React** programming model: your components stay plain React, and they resume. That combination is what React and Next.js cannot offer, since their hydration is defined as re-running components — so this is resumability you can adopt without leaving React.

chunks.title: Turn it on
What happens
chunks.text:
## What happens

- **No hydration on load.** The server renders each client island into a layout-neutral wrapper the page root *adopts but never executes* — so no component runs at load. The page is interactive immediately.
- **Resume on first interaction.** A single delegated listener catches the first event, hydrates just that island (running its component, adopting its state), and *replays the event* so your real `onClick` fires. Only the island you touched wakes up.
- **State is transported, not recomputed.** Pair it with `useSignal`/`useStore` and the server value is adopted on resume instead of re-deriving it.

> Resumability is **off by default**. A route keeps normal hydration until it sets `resumable`, and an app that never opts in bundles none of the resumability runtime.

chunks.title: What the markup looks like
chunks.text:
## What the markup looks like Nothing exotic ends up in the DOM — a resumable island is a plain wrapper with `data-*` attributes, the same shape as the rest of denext output (no custom elements). Each island's server HTML is nested in a layout-neutral `
`, its interactive elements carry a `data-dnx-h` attribute listing their event types, and one JSON script holds the trees the client resumes from: ```html
``` The wrapper uses `display:contents`, so it adds no box and does not affect layout. The page root adopts it but treats its contents as foreign — a separate per-island hydration owns them when the island resumes.

chunks.title: Serializable state — `useSignal` / `useStore`
Handlers code-split automatically
Explicit control — `qrl`
Choosing when islands wake
When to reach for it
chunks.text:
## When to reach for it

Resumability pays off wherever up-front hydration is the bottleneck. It is opt-in per route, so turn it on where it helps and leave the rest of your app on normal hydration.

- **Large, interactive pages** — dashboards, editors, feeds, data tables with many widgets. Hydration wakes all of them on load; resumption wakes only the ones a visitor touches, so time-to-interactive stays flat as the page grows instead of climbing with every widget you add.
- **Content with sparse interactivity** — long articles or marketing pages with a few interactive pieces. Ship the HTML instantly and pay for a widget only if the reader actually uses it.
- **Slow devices and cold loads** — the hydration pass is exactly the main-thread work that makes a fresh page feel janky on a phone. Removing it is the most direct win for first-load responsiveness.

When *not* to bother: a small or mostly-static page will not notice the difference, and it does add a few moving parts (a per-island runtime chunk, the delegated listener). Reach for it when the interactive surface is genuinely large or the audience is latency-sensitive — not by default on every route.

> Resumable mode applies to routes that use the client/server (Flight) boundary — any app with a `"use client"` component. Events that do not bubble (e.g. raw `focus`/`blur`) are not caught by the delegated listener; use their bubbling forms (`onFocus` maps to `focusin`).

Every recipe is `app/<path>/route.ts` exporting one function per HTTP method
(`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`). A method the
module does not export answers `405` with an `Allow` header listing the ones it
does; `HEAD` is derived from `GET` when you export only `GET`. The request body
is capped at 1 MiB unless the module says otherwise
(`export const maxBodyBytes = N | false`) — an over-cap `Content-Length` is a
`413` before the handler runs, and a chunked body past the cap errors the stream
as you read it. A typed, validated handler is [`defineApi`](/docs/typed-api);
the recipes here are the cases that are about the wire, not the schema.

Server-Sent Events
Long-running streaming (an AI completion)
WebSocket upgrade
CORS preflight by hand
When to use Live channels instead
chunks.text:
## When to use Live channels instead

Reach for a raw stream or socket when the _client_ is not a denext page: a CLI,
a mobile app, a third party, a browser `EventSource` you do not control. When
the consumer is your own `"use client"` component,
[`createChannel`](/docs/typed-api#server-push--createchannel)

- `useChannel` gives you what the recipes above leave to you — a required
  `authorize` that re-runs on a TTL, per-connection caps, latest-wins
  back-pressure, one socket per page shared by every subscription, and
  cross-instance fan-out through a `ChannelTransport` — and
  [`defineSubscription`](/docs/typed-api#typed-live-queries--usesubscription)
  re-pushes a validated query when its tags are invalidated. See
  [Live components](/docs/live).

See also: [Typed API](/docs/typed-api) for validated handlers and the typed
client, [File uploads](/docs/uploads) for multipart bodies and the caps, and the
[production checklist](/docs/production-checklist) for the deadline and body-cap
keys.

chunks.title: Conventions
chunks.text:
## Conventions

```text
app/
  layout.tsx        root layout (wraps everything)
  template.tsx      like a layout, but re-mounted on every navigation
  page.tsx          /
  loading.tsx       Suspense fallback for the segment
  error.tsx         error boundary (a "use client" component)
  global-error.tsx  root error boundary — replaces the whole tree
  not-found.tsx     404 UI
  forbidden.tsx     403 UI (forbidden())
  unauthorized.tsx  401 UI (unauthorized())
  blog/
    [slug]/page.tsx /blog/:slug
  api/
    hello/route.ts  GET/POST/... returning a Response
middleware.ts       runs before routing (proxy.ts is the same hook)
```

chunks.title: Dynamic segments
Route handlers
Navigation
chunks.text:
## Navigation

Client navigation is a soft (SPA) transition that reconciles in place; a page with no interactivity still ships no JavaScript and navigates via full requests. Everything below is exported from `denext`; the hooks are for `"use client"` components.

chunks.title: `Link`
`useRouter` — programmatic navigation
Reading the URL
Active links
Navigating after a Server Action
Typed routes
chunks.text:
### Typed routes

`denext build` and `denext dev` write `.denext/routes.ts`: `Routes` (every page path, dynamic segments as `${string}`), `ApiRoutes`, `RouteParams` and `ParamsOf<R>`. Importing the file once registers the routes with denext, and from then on:

- `<Link href>`, `router.push`/`replace` and `redirect()` only accept real paths — a typo is a compile error.
- The object form is checked too: `{ pathname: "/blog/[slug]", params: { slug } }` requires the params the pattern needs and fills it for you.
- `useParams<"/blog/[slug]">()` is `{ slug: string }`.

```tsx
import "./.denext/routes.ts"; // once, anywhere (e.g. app/layout.tsx) — registers the routes
import type { ParamsOf, Routes } from "./.denext/routes.ts";

const go = (href: Routes) => router.push(href);              // only real paths compile
router.push({ pathname: "/blog/[slug]", params: { slug } });  // → /blog/<slug>
type BlogParams = ParamsOf<"/blog/[slug]">;                    // { slug: string }
const { slug } = useParams<"/blog/[slug]">();                  // typed
```

Nothing changes at runtime; before the import, `href` is a plain `string` and the object form is the loose Next.js `UrlObject`.

chunks.title: Middleware

chunks.text:
A living catalogue of the security vulnerabilities that have affected
**Next.js**, **React / React Server Components**, and the **React tooling
ecosystem**, mapped to whether **denext** is protected against the same class of
attack.

denext reimplements the Next.js surface (App Router, SSR, middleware, image
optimization, Server Actions, RSC/Flight) on Deno with **its own tiny
React-equivalent** and **zero runtime npm dependencies**. So most published CVEs
are not a dependency-bump problem for us — they are a question of "does our
reimplementation share the vulnerable behavior?" This guide answers that, CVE by
CVE.

> **Status:** first compilation — 2026-08-10; carried forward through **2.0.0**,
> last reviewed **2026-09-05** (the pre-2.0.0 whole-app audit) after the review
> against the Next.js **August 2026 security release** (2026-08-25). Every
> [Known Gap](#known-gaps--residual-risk) is closed or mitigated, plus an
> **August-2026 review pass** that added eleven new parity tests: the two new
> August advisories (CVE-2026-75604 Windows-FS RCE, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4
> AVIF/libheif RCE) and nine back-propagated / previously-`⚪`-review rows, all
> now covered in `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`. A **round-2 pass
> (2026-08-29)** added ten more: a new
> **[§15 first-party-auth](#15-first-party-auth--next-auth--authjs-cve-parity)**
> table back-propagating the next-auth / Auth.js / `jsonwebtoken` CVE class
> against denext's own OAuth/OIDC/JWT/session code (`tests/auth*.test.ts`,
> `tests/session.test.ts`), plus two fresh 2026 Next.js CVEs (CVE-2026-29057
> rewrite smuggling, CVE-2026-27980 image disk-cache DoS). All assessed
> **already immune** — regression tests, no fix. CVE data was gathered from
> public advisory databases (see [Sources](#sources)); 2026 advisory numbers
> should be re-verified against primary sources before being used to set
> remediation SLAs. Protection verdicts come from a source-level audit, the live
> `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts` suite, and the per-feature tests noted in
> each row.

---

chunks.title: How to read the "Protection Level" column
chunks.text:
## How to read the "Protection Level" column

| Badge                             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ✅ **Protected (tested)**         | denext refuses the exact exploit **and** a live parity/regression test asserts it (`tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts` or `tests/safe-fetch.test.ts`).                                     |
| 🟢 **Protected (by design)**      | denext's architecture makes the class unreachable (e.g. it never proxies a rewrite, ships no npm deps, has no Turbopack), verified by source audit but without a dedicated exploit test. |
| 🟡 **Partial / config-dependent** | A guard exists but coverage depends on user configuration or a documented developer responsibility; or one sub-case is unguarded.                                                        |
| 🔵 **N/A — feature absent**       | denext does not implement the vulnerable feature or ship the vulnerable dependency, so the CVE cannot apply.                                                                             |
| 🔴 **Gap**                        | denext implements the feature and currently has **no** guard — real residual risk, tracked in [Known Gaps](#known-gaps--residual-risk).                                                  |
| ⚪ **Needs review**               | Not yet assessed — tracked in [Known Gaps](#known-gaps--residual-risk) until it is.                                                                                                      |

---

chunks.title: Why denext is structurally immune to a large share of the ecosystem's CVEs
chunks.text:
## Why denext is structurally immune to a large share of the ecosystem's CVEs

Before the tables — the architectural facts that make many rows `🔵 N/A`:

1. **Zero runtime npm dependencies.** The entire class of "transitive
   dependency" CVEs that dominate `npm audit` on a Create-React-App / Next.js
   project simply does not exist here. No `webpack-dev-server`, `immer`,
   `nth-check`, `node-forge`, `serialize-javascript`, `react-dev-utils`,
   `@react-native-community/cli`, etc.
2. **Own React-equivalent.** React-core and `react-server-dom-*` CVEs apply only
   if we reproduced the vulnerable code. Our Flight parser is a purely
   structural decoder (no `eval`/`Function`), which is exactly the property the
   RCE CVEs violate.
3. **denext never acts as a proxy.** Rewrites re-route by pathname against the
   local manifest; redirects and Server-Action redirects are returned to the
   client as 3xx. The server never fetches a request-derived destination —
   closing an entire SSRF family by construction.
4. **No Turbopack, no Edge runtime, no `/_next/data` JSON routes, and no client
   streaming-resume / `Next-Resume` protocol.** Several 2026 Next.js CVEs are
   specific to those subsystems. (denext _does_ implement Cache Components / PPR
   — the stable `cacheComponents` opt-in — but resumes dynamic holes by buffered
   server-side splice, not the streaming-resume mechanism the Cache-Components
   CVE targets.)
5. **Deno permission model.** The process runs under explicit `--allow-*`
   grants; an RCE or path-traversal that did land is still boxed by the sandbox
   the user granted.

The flip side: a few things are **our** responsibility precisely _because_ we
reimplement them — see [Known Gaps](#known-gaps--residual-risk).

---

chunks.title: 1. Middleware / authorization bypass
chunks.text:
## 1. Middleware / authorization bypass

| CVE / Advisory     | Description                                                                                                                                                                             | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CVE-2025-29927** | Middleware auth bypass via the trusted internal `x-middleware-subrequest` header — send it externally and Next.js skips middleware entirely (reach `/admin` unauthenticated). CVSS 9.1. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext's runner fires unconditionally on every request; **no** inbound `x-middleware-*` header is ever read from the client, and the internal markers are stripped before responses leave. Parity test fires every documented header shape incl. the multi-segment chain variant.     |
| **CVE-2024-51479** | Authorization bypass for pages directly under the app root — pathname-based middleware auth could be skipped for `/foo`. CVSS 7.5.                                                      | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — middleware runs on all paths including root; `//x` and `/x/` are 308-canonicalized before matching and a matcher's trailing slash is optional, so no spelling of a guarded path skips the guard. `tests/middleware.test.ts`, `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                       |
| **CVE-2026-64642** | Middleware/proxy bypass with a single i18n locale (Turbopack): crafted requests circumvent auth. CVSS 8.3.                                                                              | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — middleware runs on locale-prefixed paths AND its `matcher` is tested against the locale-STRIPPED path (Next's semantics), so `/admin/:path*` guards `/fr/admin` too; a locale prefix can't route around a path-restricted middleware. `tests/middleware.test.ts`.                     |
| **CVE-2026-44573** | Pages-Router i18n data routes (`/_next/data/<buildId>/<page>.json`) escape middleware. CVSS 7.5.                                                                                        | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext has no `/_next/data` JSON route; a data-shaped variant (`/secret.json`, `/secret.rsc`, `/_next/data/…`) of a protected path either 404s or is gated by the SAME middleware, never a bypass that serves the page's data. `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                     |
| **CVE-2026-44574** | Dynamic-route parameter injection: malicious query params alter the resolved route value while still passing middleware authorization. CVSS 8.1.                                        | 🟢 **Protected (by design)** — route params come ONLY from the matched pattern's segments (`src/router/match.ts`); the query string never participates in route resolution, and middleware and the renderer match the same canonicalized pathname through one dispatcher, so there is no param-driven divergence. |
| **CVE-2026-44575** | App Router segment-prefetch bypass: crafted `.rsc`/segment-prefetch URL variants resolve to a protected page without matching the middleware rule. CVSS 7.5.                            | 🟢 **Protected (by design)** — denext has no `.rsc`/segment-prefetch URL variants: a soft navigation requests the SAME URL with an `x-denext-nav: 1` header and goes through the same pipeline (middleware included), so no URL spelling reaches a page whose matcher did not fire.                               |
| **CVE-2026-45109** | Turbopack-only incomplete-fix follow-up to 44575. CVSS 7.5.                                                                                                                             | 🔵 **N/A** — denext has no Turbopack build path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

chunks.title: 2. Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
chunks.text:
## 2. Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

| CVE / Advisory                          | Description                                                                                                                                               | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CVE-2024-34351**                      | SSRF in Server Actions via the `Host` header — a relative redirect makes the self-hosted server issue requests to itself. CVSS 7.5.                       | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext returns a client 3xx from actions and never performs a server-side fetch of the target; Server-Action CSRF parity test covers this.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **CVE-2025-57822**                      | SSRF via `NextResponse.next({headers})` — a `Location` header on a `next()` outcome is treated as a redirect and fetched by the server. CVSS 6.5.         | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — a `Location` on a `next()` outcome is not server-fetched; the page renders normally.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **CVE-2026-64645**                      | SSRF/open-redirect in `rewrites()`/`redirects()` when the destination **hostname** is built from request input. CVSS 8.3.                                 | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext re-routes rewrites by pathname against the local manifest and never proxies out to a request-derived host.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **CVE-2026-64649**                      | SSRF in Server Actions on custom servers — a forwarded/redirecting action sends the outbound request to an attacker's host. CVSS 8.3.                     | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — action redirects return a client 3xx, never a server fetch.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **CVE-2026-44578**                      | WebSocket-upgrade SSRF — self-hosted apps proxy WS upgrade requests to internal destinations (metadata endpoints). CVSS 8.6.                              | 🟢 **Protected (by design)** — the only WebSocket proxy is SPA mode's `spa.proxy`, which forwards a configured prefix to the ONE configured `target` (never a request-derived host) and forwards the browser's own `Origin` rather than forging one; the Live hub is a fixed same-origin endpoint. Live reload is SSE, not a WebSocket.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **`_next/image` SSRF family** (general) | The image optimizer fetching attacker-chosen `?url=` targets — the long-running Next.js image-SSRF history, incl. redirect-to-metadata and DNS-rebinding. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — remote fetch gated by `remotePatterns`/`domains` allowlist, http(s)-only, **per-redirect-hop** revalidation, and `safeFetch` DNS-pinning that refuses if **any** resolved A/AAAA is loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/multicast (incl. `169.254.169.254`). IPv6 is parsed properly (`::` expansion, embedded IPv4), so the **IPv4-mapped** (`::ffff:7f00:1`), IPv4-compatible, and NAT64 (`64:ff9b::`) forms route through the IPv4 block-list too — closing the string-prefix bypass (SEC-C1); a full IPv6 parity matrix tests it. `safeFetch` is exported for app use on untrusted URLs; a decode-free header probe also rejects decompression-bomb dimensions before decode (SEC-M1). |

chunks.title: 3. React Server Components / Flight protocol (RCE, DoS, source leak)
chunks.text:
## 3. React Server Components / Flight protocol (RCE, DoS, source leak)

> The single most dangerous modern cluster. denext ships its own Flight
> implementation, so the question is purely whether our decoder shares the flaw.

| CVE / Advisory                                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CVE-2025-55182** (React) / **CVE-2025-66478** (Next.js) — "React2Shell"              | Unauthenticated **RCE (CVSS 10.0)** via unsafe deserialization of Flight chunks that resolve into the `Function` constructor; crafted POST to any Server Function endpoint. Actively exploited. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext's `parseFlight` is a purely structural decoder: it dispatches on a `$` discriminant, builds VNodes via `h(...)`, and resolves components/actions by **id lookup in a build-assigned registry**. No `eval`, no `Function`, no payload-driven import. A server-reference-shaped payload decodes to inert data and is never invoked.                                                                     |
| **CVE-2025-55184** → **CVE-2025-67779** (incomplete-fix follow-up); **CVE-2026-23864** | DoS: crafted request to any App Router endpoint hangs the process in an infinite deserialization loop. Vulnerable even with no Server Functions defined. CVSS 7.5.                              | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — a deeply nested payload is bounded (`JSON.parse` throws and is caught → no hang); a `__proto__` in the payload does not pollute `Object.prototype`; oversized action bodies are refused 413 before the handler runs.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **CVE-2025-55183**                                                                     | Source-code exposure — a crafted request makes the server stringify and return a Server Function's raw JS source (leaking inlined secrets). CVSS 5.3.                                           | 🟢 **Protected (by design)** — actions are resolved by a `Map` id lookup and never stringified back to the client; args deserialize with no reviver/eval. _(Add a regression test — see backlog.)_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **CVE-2026-23869 / CVE-2026-23870 / CVE-2026-44907**                                   | Recurring RSC/Server-Function resource-exhaustion DoS (unbounded CPU/memory, missing throttling — CWE-400/770). CVSS 7.5.                                                                       | 🟡 **Partial** — structural parsing + a 413 body cap (`actionMaxBodyBytes` in `denext.config.ts`, default **1 MiB**) + a **slow-body idle timeout** (→ 408) blunt the payload/trickle vectors; the `requestTimeout` deadline (config key or `DENEXT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, **default 30 s**, armed across a streamed body) bounds a runaway handler. A per-request CPU budget + connection-slot ceiling remain deployment-layer by design. |

> **Trust model — Flight props are not tainted.** Any prop a Server Component
> passes to a Client Component is serialized into the Flight payload and shipped
> to the browser, exactly as in React/Next.js's RSC model. denext does **no**
> taint tracking and cannot detect a secret crossing that boundary. The rule is
> the standard RSC one: **do not pass secrets (API keys, tokens, other users'
> data, raw DB rows) as props into a Client Component** — keep them on the
> server and pass only what the client needs to render. This is a design
> property, not a bug: the server/client boundary is a trust boundary the author
> is responsible for.

chunks.title: 4. Server Actions (DoS / abuse)
chunks.text:
## 4. Server Actions (DoS / abuse)

| CVE / Advisory     | Description                                                                                                                                          | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CVE-2024-56332** | Hanging Server Action invocations ("denial of wallet") via bad `Content-Length` / unclosed connections; low resource use evades detection. CVSS 5.3. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — body size is hard-capped (declared `Content-Length` fast-path + streamed cap → 413) **and** the body reader now aborts on a per-chunk idle timeout (default 30s) → 408, so a trickled/never-closed body cannot pin a handler. `tests/server-action.test.ts`.                                                                                                                               |
| **CVE-2026-64641** | DoS in App Router Server Actions via unbounded iteration (CWE-834) spiking CPU and blocking the process. CVSS 8.2.                                   | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — the multipart arg decoder now validates the attacker-controlled `fdIndex` as an in-range integer of `others` before `args[fdIndex] = fd`; an out-of-range index (which would inflate the arg array so the handler's `handler(...args)` spread iterates every hole) is rejected and falls back to a single-FormData arg. `src/runtime/server-action.ts`; `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`. |
| **CVE-2026-64646** | Unbounded Server-Action payload in the **Edge** runtime exhausts memory. CVSS 6.3.                                                                   | ✅ **Protected** — action bodies are capped (`actionMaxBodyBytes` in `denext.config.ts`, default 1 MiB; over → 413) regardless of runtime; denext also has no separate Edge runtime with a different limit.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **CVE-2026-44579** | Cache Components connection-exhaustion DoS via malformed `Next-Resume` headers.                                                                      | 🔵 **N/A** — denext's Cache Components (opt-in, `cacheComponents: true`) resume dynamic holes by **buffered server-side splice**, with no client `Next-Resume` header or streaming-resume protocol, so the malformed-`Next-Resume` connection-exhaustion vector does not exist.                                                                                                                                        |

chunks.title: 5. Cache poisoning / cache confusion
chunks.text:
## 5. Cache poisoning / cache confusion

| CVE / Advisory                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CVE-2024-46982**                      | Pages-Router SSR cache poisoning — a crafted request forces an uncacheable route to be cached with `s-maxage`. CVSS 7.5.                                                                                                      | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — the soft-nav data variant (`x-denext-nav`) is fully partitioned from the ISR HTML cache: never reads it, never writes it; internal-looking headers don't fork the key.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **CVE-2025-32421**                      | Race condition — a data request racing an `x-now-route-matches` request serves `pageProps` JSON with cacheable headers (bypass of 46982). CVSS 3.7.                                                                           | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — same partition test; denext does not honor an attacker `x-now-route-matches`-style header to fork the cache.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **CVE-2025-49005** / **CVE-2026-44576** | App Router RSC/HTML cache confusion — an HTML request returns an RSC payload (or vice-versa), poisoning shared caches. CVSS 3.7 / Moderate.                                                                                   | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — HTML and soft-nav/RSC variants are partitioned; cache key is `pathname + search`, never the response variant of a different request.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **CVE-2025-49826**                      | A crafted request caches an empty **HTTP 204 / non-200**, then serves the blank page to everyone (DoS). CVSS 7.5.                                                                                                             | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — only a render with status **exactly 200** is ever stored; a 404/redirect/empty render re-renders each time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **CVE-2026-64647**                      | Cache confusion of `fetch` response bodies containing **invalid UTF-8** — different bodies share a cache key. CVSS 6.3.                                                                                                       | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — `cachedFetch` buffers a non-string body to bytes before keying; string bodies were already keyed correctly. _(Confirm invalid-UTF-8 string bodies key distinctly — see backlog.)_                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **CVE-2026-64648**                      | Cache confusion via `fetch(new Request(init), otherInit)` — same URL, different bodies share one cache entry, leaking response data. CVSS 6.0.                                                                                | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — same body-keying fix; distinct bodies get distinct entries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **CVE-2024-34350**                      | HTTP request smuggling in `rewrites` — inconsistent parsing desyncs the response queue between users. CVSS 7.5.                                                                                                               | 🟢 **Protected (by design + tested framing)** — denext never proxies rewrites; and `safeFetch`'s hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 client enforces strict `Content-Length` framing and Transfer-Encoding precedence (request-smuggling fuzz tests in `safe-fetch.test.ts`).                                                                                                                                    |
| **CVE-2026-29057**                      | HTTP request smuggling in `rewrites` — a `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` DELETE/OPTIONS to a rewritten route desyncs the proxy↔backend request boundary, smuggling a second request to an internal/admin backend route. CWE-444. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext never proxies a rewrite to a backend: it re-routes by the destination **pathname** against the local manifest and issues no outbound request, so there is no proxy↔backend framing to disagree on. A chunked DELETE/OPTIONS/POST to a rewritten path is handled locally (no `fetch`); the GET resolves to the local target. `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`. |
| **CVE-2023-46298**                      | Missing `Cache-Control` on prefetch responses → CDN caches empty responses and serves them to all users (DoS). CVSS 7.5.                                                                                                      | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — soft-nav / Flight responses carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store` so a shared CDN never caches a partial/empty variant, and every navigable response now carries `Vary: x-denext-nav` so a cache keys the soft/hard variants apart. `tests/flight-nav.test.ts`, `tests/security-headers.test.ts`.                                                                  |
| **CVE-2026-44572**                      | Middleware redirect cache poisoning — injecting `x-nextjs-data` makes middleware emit an internal header instead of a `Location`, caching broken redirects. CVSS 3.7.                                                         | 🟢 **Protected (by design)** — denext strips internal `x-middleware-*` markers before responses leave and does not branch redirect behavior on a client header. _(Add a regression test.)_                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **CVE-2026-44582**                      | Weak `_rsc` cache-busting hash → collisions let an attacker make users receive the wrong response variant. CVSS 3.7.                                                                                                          | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext partitions soft/hard navigations by the `x-denext-nav` **request header**, not a guessable URL token, and the soft variant is `private, no-store` (no shared-cache entry for a weak-hash collision to poison); a Next-style `?_rsc=…` token is ignored and does not fork the variant. `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                                       |

chunks.title: 6. Image optimizer (DoS / content injection / info-leak)
chunks.text:
## 6. Image optimizer (DoS / content injection / info-leak)

| CVE / Advisory                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                  | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CVE-2021-39178** / **CVE-2022-23646** | XSS / CSP-spoofing via user SVGs served through the image optimizer. CVSS 6.1 / 7.5.                                                                                                         | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — the image endpoint **never** emits `image/svg+xml`; output is always a raster format (webp, or avif when enabled) — or plain text for errors.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **CVE-2025-55173**                      | Content injection / arbitrary file download — a crafted upstream response bypasses content-type checks to force a download under the trusted origin. CVSS 4.3.                               | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — the endpoint never sets `Content-Disposition` and never serves `text/html`; only image or text/plain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **CVE-2024-47831** / **CVE-2026-44577** | Image-optimization DoS via uncontrolled recursion / decompression bombs — CPU exhaustion. CVSS 5.9 / Moderate.                                                                               | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — the requested width must be one of a small **allowlist** (`images.deviceSizes` ∪ `imageSizes`, Next's standard set by default) — rejected `400` **before** any decode, so an attacker can't spray unbounded distinct widths; concurrent optimizations are capped by a semaphore; download bounded (25 MiB, declared + streamed) with a fetch timeout; and a decompression-bomb guard rejects sources past a dimension (12 000) / pixel (40 M) cap **before** resize. `tests/image.test.ts`, `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`. |
| **CVE-2026-64644**                      | Image-optimization DoS via malicious **SVGs** forcing CPU exhaustion on `/_next/image`. CVSS 6.3.                                                                                            | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — an SVG **source** is now refused outright: the optimizer sniffs the leading bytes and returns `400` before the decode (the endpoint emits only raster webp/avif, and an SVG can smuggle active script, so it is never rasterized or echoed). `src/server/image-optimizer.ts`; `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4** _(Aug 2026)_    | Unauthenticated **RCE** via a crafted **AVIF** input decoded by `libheif` (through `sharp`) in Next.js Image Optimization; patched Next disables AVIF until upstream fixes land.             | 🟢 **Protected (by design + tested)** — denext ships **no `sharp`/`libheif`**: it decodes with wasm `@denext/photon` and only ever _encodes_ AVIF via first-party wasm `@denext/avif`. AVIF is never a decode target (`probeImageDimensions` doesn't recognize it) and `negotiateFormat` selects AVIF **only** when a route both configures `formats:["image/avif"]` **and** the client sends `Accept: image/avif`, so the native-heif decode path is unreachable and off by default. Deno also sandboxes wasm. `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.         |
| **CVE-2025-57752**                      | Image cache-key confusion — `Cookie`/`Authorization` forwarded to the internal image route but ignored in the cache key, leaking user-specific images. CVSS 6.2.                             | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — `fetchRemoteImage` takes only a URL and builds its own header-free outbound init (it cannot forward the inbound request's `Cookie`/`Authorization`); an injected upstream sees no user credentials. There is no per-user credentialed internal image fetch to key incorrectly. `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **CVE-2026-27980**                      | `/_next/image` disk-cache exhaustion — Next.js wrote an optimized variant to disk for every distinct `?w`/`?q` with no bound/eviction, so spraying widths/qualities fills the disk. CWE-400. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — denext bounds the variant space: an out-of-allowlist **width** is `400`'d before any file is read (`deviceSizes ∪ imageSizes`, tested), and **quality** is coerced to the small `qualities` allowlist (`coerceQuality`), so the distinct `(w,q)` cardinality is finite and an attacker cannot spray unbounded cache entries. `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                |

chunks.title: 7. Cross-site scripting (rendering)
chunks.text:
## 7. Cross-site scripting (rendering)

| CVE / Advisory                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **React CVE-2018-6341**                                                                       | `ReactDOMServer` did not escape user-supplied **attribute names**; spreading attacker-controlled prop keys during SSR breaks out of the attribute context. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — `isValidAttrName` rejects any name containing whitespace/quotes/`<>/=`/control chars **and any `on*` name (case-insensitive)** — a single chokepoint shared by all three SSR renderers and the client reconciler's `setAttribute`. A parity test spreads hostile prop keys (`"x onload=alert(1)"`, `"a><script>…"`, `onMouseOver`, a quote-breakout name) through SSR and asserts none survive. `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                  |
| **denext 0.8.1 hardening** (lowercase `on*` XSS)                                              | Lowercase HTML-native handlers (`onmouseover`, `onerror`) spread from untrusted props were emitted as live event-handler attributes during SSR.            | ✅ **Protected (fixed + tested)** — handler filtering is now case-insensitive at the shared `isValidAttrName` chokepoint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **CVE-2018-18282**                                                                            | Reflected XSS through the `/_error` (404/500) page.                                                                                                        | 🟢 **Protected (by design)** — the built-in 404 strips `<`/`>`/`&` from the reflected path (`src/server/response-headers.ts`), the production 500 reflects nothing (a fixed body + an opaque digest), and the dev error page escapes every field it prints.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **CVE-2026-44580**                                                                            | XSS in `beforeInteractive` scripts — serialized script content wasn't HTML-escaped, allowing breakout. CVSS 6.1.                                           | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — every framework-serialized inline island (`__denext_data`, `__denext_islands`, `__denext_state`, public-env, Flight, JSON-LD) escapes `<` → `\u003c`, so request-derived data (params/searchParams) placed into an inline `<script>` can never form a `</script>` breakout — a parity test drives a hostile searchParam through `renderDocument` and asserts the escape. An app's own `<Script>` inline body stays verbatim **by design** (the developer owns its safety, exactly as `next/script` + `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`). `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`. |
| **CVE-2026-44581**                                                                            | Stored XSS via malformed CSP **nonce** values reflected from request headers into rendered HTML. CVSS 4.7.                                                 | ✅ **Protected (tested / by design)** — denext's CSP is **hash-based, never nonce-based** (`src/server/csp.ts`): `script-src` is exactly `'self'` plus per-route opt-ins, derived from content, and **no request header populates it** — so there is no reflected nonce to poison. A parity test asserts `computeCsp` emits no `nonce-` source and reflects no request-derived value. (Should nonce support ever be added, it must validate before reflecting.) `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`.                                                                                              |
| **`javascript:` URI in `href`/`src`/`formAction`** _(React attack pattern; not a formal CVE)_ | React escapes attribute _values_ but does not sanitize URL **schemes**; `href="javascript:alert(1)"` from user input executes. React 16.9+ only _warns_.   | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — `sanitizeUrlAttr` (SSR renderers + client `setAttribute`) drops `javascript:`/`vbscript:` in any URL attribute and executable `data:` in navigable/scripty contexts, defeating whitespace/control-char obfuscation; a dev-only warning fires. `tests/url-scheme.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with untrusted HTML** _(React attack pattern; not a formal CVE)_  | The API bypasses escaping by design; unsanitized user input → direct XSS. The most common React XSS sink.                                                  | 🟡 **By design (developer responsibility) — now warned.** Emitted raw for React parity, but denext now emits a dev-only warning (SSR + client) pointing at a sanitizer, and applies the HTML correctly on the client. `tests/dangerous-html.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

chunks.title: 8. Path traversal
chunks.text:
## 8. Path traversal

| CVE / Advisory                                            | Description                                                                                                                                             | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **CVE-2017-16877**                                        | Directory traversal in early ZEIT Next.js — read files outside the intended dir.                                                                        | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — `serveStatic` decodes then enforces lexical containment within `publicDir` across encoding tricks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **CVE-2018-6184**                                         | Directory traversal under the `/_next` namespace (CWE-22). CVSS 7.5.                                                                                    | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — same containment guard; denext serves build assets from prefixed synthetic endpoints, not by filesystem path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **CVE-2020-5284**                                         | Path traversal into the `.next`/build-output directory. CVSS 4.3.                                                                                       | ✅ **Protected** — the dev/prod servers expose only specific `/_denext/*` endpoints from in-memory bundler output; there is no `readFile(url.pathname)` sink. Plus a **symlink-escape** guard: a symlink inside `public/` resolving outside it (via `Deno.realPath`) is refused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **CVE-2026-75604** / **GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36** _(Aug 2026)_ | Unauthenticated **RCE** on Windows-hosted Next.js (Pages+App Router without Cache Components) via a Windows-separator path traversal. CWE-22, CVSS 9.0. | 🟢 **Protected (by design + tested)** — denext has no dual Pages+App legacy cache-path and no Windows-only route resolver, so the RCE mechanism is absent by construction. The underlying traversal is closed regardless of separator: `serveStatic` enforces lexical containment with the **platform** separator, so backslash / `..\..\` / UNC (`\\host\share`) / drive-letter (`C:\`) / mixed-encoding (`..%2f..%5c`) escapes never resolve outside `publicDir`. `src/server/static.ts`; `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`. |

chunks.title: 9. Open redirect
chunks.text:
## 9. Open redirect

| CVE / Advisory                                    | Description                                                                                                                | Protection Level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CVE-2021-37699**                                | Open redirect — a crafted URL redirects to an attacker destination.                                                        | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — config/framework redirects funnel through `safeRedirectLocation`, which collapses protocol-relative escapes (`//host`, `/\host`, `\/\/host`, `///host`) to a single-slash same-origin path while preserving explicit absolute URLs.                                                                                                                                                       |
| **react-router CVE-2026-40181**                   | Open redirect via a path starting with `//` reinterpreted by the browser as protocol-relative. CVSS Moderate.              | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — `safeRedirectLocation` neutralizes exactly this; client `navigate`/`prefetch` fall back to full navigation cross-origin and only prefetch same-origin.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **react-router CVE-2026-22029 / CVE-2026-53668**  | XSS via `javascript:` (or open-redirect→XSS) returned from a loader/action redirect because the protocol wasn't validated. | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — a `javascript:` `Location` is inert (not browser-navigable); framework redirects also normalize through `safeRedirectLocation` (a `javascript:`/`vbscript:` target becomes an inert same-origin path, verified end-to-end through `handleAction`), and the URL-scheme filter drops `javascript:` from any rendered `href`/`formAction` (client + SSR). `tests/nextjs-cve-parity.test.ts`. |
| **CVE-2026-44572** (redirect side)                | See [§5](#5-cache-poisoning--cache-confusion) — internal-header-driven redirect poisoning.                                 | 🟢 **Protected (by design)** — internal markers stripped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Manual `middleware.redirect(location)` helper** | A redirect helper whose `Location` could be an open-redirect sharp edge if `location` is user-controlled.                  | ✅ **Protected (tested)** — the `redirectResponse()` middleware helper (`src/server/middleware.ts`) normalizes `location` through `safeRedirectLocation` before emitting it, so protocol-relative escapes collapse to a same-origin path automatically.
